rows.quote: It opened in nineteen sixty-seven, a few years after the islanders came home. They named it Calshot, after the village in England that took them in.
rows.statement: Tristan da Cunha's Calshot Harbour opened in 1967 and is named after Calshot in Hampshire, England, where the evacuated islanders were housed in 1962–63.

nguon.title: Calshot Harbour
nguon.publisher: Tristan da Cunha Government & Tristan da Cunha Association

rows.quote: The entrance is about eleven metres wide, roughly thirty-six feet. And the island government reckons the weather lets boats in and out safely on only about seventy days a year. Think of a shop that opens about one day in five, and never says which.
rows.statement: Calshot Harbour on Tristan da Cunha has an entrance about 11 m (36 ft) wide; according to the Tristan da Cunha Government, weather makes it safe for boats to enter and leave on only about 70 days a year (other sources give about 60 or 90).

rows.quote: In twenty oh eight, the fish factory burned down and took the island's power station with it. Full power took about a month to come back.
rows.statement: On the night of 12–13 February 2008 Tristan da Cunha's fish factory burned down together with the island's electricity generators; full 24-hour power was restored on 14 March 2008, about a month later.

rows.statement: Outsiders cannot buy land on Tristan da Cunha, and people without a family connection to the island are not normally allowed to settle there.
